01 · The Problem

One missed number on a drawing can stall a billion-dollar data-centre build.

Every submittal for a hyperscale build must match hundreds of pages of structural and electrical code. Today a senior engineer checks that by hand, and a single overlooked clause means months of rework, or a facility that isn't safe to power on.

A footing poured at 30 mm cover, against the 50 mm legal minimum (IS 456:2000, Cl. 26.4.2.2). By the time a human catches it, the concrete has set.
Industry context, not a SiteMind metric: 67% of data-centre EPC projects in Asia-Pacific overrun schedule by more than 10% (Turner & Townsend, 2024), led by procurement misalignment and commissioning failures.
02 · The Gap We Found

Manual review is too slow. Generic AI tools guess.

Manual review
A senior engineer reads hundreds of pages by hand, days per document, and still misses what humans miss.
Naïve RAG chatbots
Retrieve a paragraph and let a language model decide if it's compliant, with no abstention gate and no guardrail against a fabricated citation.
Spreadsheets & checklists
Static, don't scale to hundreds of IS clauses, and can't link an issue to the RFI, schedule task, and shipment it touches.
03 · The Idea

The model never decides.

An LLM reads the document and writes the report. The pass-or-fail call is made by deterministic Python, against a real, cited Indian-standard clause. Auditable, reproducible, impossible to fake.

04 · Perceive → Decide → Explain

Three stages. A model touches only the outer two.

1 · Perceive
Read & extract
Claude Sonnet 4.6 pulls each parameter with its exact source span, behind a deterministic span-verification gate, or abstains.
→
2 · Decide
Check the clause
Deterministic Python tests the value against the cited IS/CEA clause. Re-runnable, and the one step a model may never touch.
→
3 · Explain
Write the finding
The model drafts the non-conformance in plain English, around a decision it did not make.

Every citation resolves to real primary-source text, digitised IS and CEA codes, never paraphrased from model memory, and each clause discloses its own reliability tier.

05 · Architecture

LLM-first where intelligence matters. Deterministic where trust matters.

The intelligence layer

Claude Sonnet 4.6, via the Claude Agent SDK. Reads and extracts from documents, answers cross-document questions, and writes every finding. This is where the product feels smart.

The guarantee layer

Deterministic Python. Owns the compliance verdict and resolves every citation to real clause text. A verdict or a citation can never be fabricated.

06 · One shared graph, five disciplines (1/2)

Compliance, Copilot, Schedule

Compliance Agent
Catches design non-conformances before casting or procurement, cited against real IS/CEA clauses.
Project Copilot
Guardrailed hybrid retrieval — BM25 + dense, reciprocal-rank fused — detects previously-resolved RFIs and abstains below a deterministic floor instead of guessing.
Schedule Risk
Recomputes critical-path slip against weather and workforce, with three mitigation agents.
07 · One shared graph, five disciplines (2/2)

Supply Chain, Commissioning, Timeline

Supply Chain
Traces component latency three tiers deep, with computed viable alternatives before it hits critical path.
Commissioning QA
Deterministic pass / allowable / fail against the ASHRAE cooling envelope, from a real test log.
Project Timeline
Every finding, RFI, risk, and alert on one cross-linked view. Pure aggregation, zero new judgement.
Electrical/fire commissioning is deferred on a disclosed corpus gap, not shipped as complete.
08 · No vector database needed

Traced, not guessed.

Retrieval, where it runs, is guardrailed hybrid search with a deterministic abstention gate. But the cross-pillar memory is a NetworkX graph, not a vector store: a permanent, clickable link that traces a parameter to the physical asset, the RFI, and the schedule task it affects — never an unstable similarity guess.

Structural Submittal SHP-002 ↔ RFI-EL-112 ↔ Schedule Task DC1-04-EL-030
09 · The standards backbone

A verified-standards layer any agent can call.

Codebook  ·  MCP service

A standalone standards service running its own MCP server over streamable-HTTP, exposing search_standards, get_clause, and list_corpora. SiteMind consumes it as a client — and so can any other tool in an EPC stack.

6,206 verbatim-verified chunks · 17 real Indian codes · a source-type reliability tier on every clause.

Knowledge Base  ·  hybrid retrieval

Guardrailed retrieval, not naïve RAG. BM25 keyword fused with dense embeddings by reciprocal-rank fusion, with a deterministic cosine floor as the abstention gate — the same discipline the Copilot runs on.

Multi-corpus, with live document upload, so a company's own submittals become searchable under the same cited, abstaining rules.

The middle stays deterministic: retrieval fuses and ranks candidates, but the go/no-go to answer is a fixed threshold — so the model never decides whether it has enough to speak.

Hours, not percentages: the Overview sums issues caught × disclosed per-issue constants (~20 hrs, ₹15L each) — labelled assumptions, not measured outcomes from a live project.

Scales without retraining

Every check maps to a real digitised clause, so breadth grows by adding a clause, never by retraining a model. No training run, no dataset to relabel, no drift.

Backbone: 6,206 verbatim-verified chunks across 17 real Indian codes, exposed over MCP for any agent to query.

11 · What's Next

The verification layer for every data centre built in India.

  • Widen the code library to IS 875, IS 13920, IS 800, and NBC 2016, the most-cited code in real permitting.
  • Extend perception to drawings with vision models, so shop drawings read the same way the text path does.
  • One backbone, many tools. The standards service speaks MCP, so any tool in an EPC stack can call the same verified codes.
